output_cleanup.title: OpenAI implements safeguards to prevent data leaks when AI agents fetch URLs by verifying links against a public web index
output_cleanup.description:
OpenAI has introduced measures to protect user data when AI agents interact with web links, addressing risks of data exfiltration through URLs and prompt injection attacks. The system checks whether a URL has been previously observed on the public web before allowing automatic fetching, reducing the chance of leaking private information.

This approach avoids relying solely on trusted site lists, which can be bypassed through redirects or cause user friction. When a URL is unverified, users receive warnings and must explicitly approve access, maintaining control over potentially sensitive data exposure. These safeguards focus on preventing quiet data leaks via URLs but do not guarantee the trustworthiness of web content or protection against social engineering.

output_cleanup.title: OpenAI and Paradigm launch EVMbench to benchmark AI agents detecting, patching, and exploiting smart contract vulnerabilities using 117 curated cases
output_cleanup.description:
OpenAI and Paradigm introduced EVMbench, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' capabilities in detecting, patching, and exploiting high-severity vulnerabilities in smart contracts. The benchmark includes 117 vulnerabilities from 40 audits and scenarios from the Tempo blockchain, focusing on payment-oriented smart contract code.

EVMbench tests AI agents across three modes: detecting vulnerabilities, patching contracts without breaking functionality, and exploiting contracts in a sandboxed environment. The benchmark uses a Rust-based harness for reproducible evaluation and has shown that newer AI models like GPT-5.3-Codex significantly outperform earlier versions in exploit tasks, though detection and patching remain challenging.

While EVMbench provides a realistic assessment environment, it does not cover all complexities of real-world smart contract security, such as timing-dependent exploits or multi-chain scenarios. The benchmark aims to encourage defensive AI use in auditing and strengthening deployed contracts securing billions in crypto assets.

output_cleanup.title: OpenAI builds internal beta software product with zero manually-written code using Codex agents over five months
output_cleanup.description:
OpenAI's engineering team developed an internal beta software product entirely generated by Codex agents without any manually-written code, completing about a million lines of code in five months. The product has daily internal users and external alpha testers, demonstrating significant engineering velocity improvements by shifting human roles from coding to designing environments and specifying intent for AI agents.

The development began with an empty repository in August 2025, with Codex generating all initial scaffolding and subsequent code, tests, documentation, and tooling. A small team of engineers focused on enabling and guiding Codex agents through prompts and iterative reviews, pushing most review tasks to agent-to-agent interactions. This approach redefined engineering work to emphasize system design and agent capability enhancement rather than direct coding.

As the project progressed, human quality assurance became the bottleneck, leading the team to improve application legibility for Codex by integrating tools like Chrome DevTools Protocol and enabling the AI to launch and test app instances per change. This experiment highlights a shift toward agent-first software development, maximizing human time and attention by leveraging AI for code generation and maintenance.

output_cleanup.title: Google DeepMind introduces Decoupled DiLoCo, a resilient distributed AI training architecture enabling asynchronous training across distant data centers with lower bandwidth and hardware fault tolerance
output_cleanup.description:
Google DeepMind has developed Decoupled DiLoCo, a new distributed AI training architecture that divides training across asynchronous compute "islands" to improve resilience and reduce bandwidth needs. This approach isolates hardware failures to maintain training progress and supports training large language models across geographically distant data centers.

Built on prior systems like Pathways and DiLoCo, Decoupled DiLoCo demonstrated fault tolerance through chaos engineering tests and achieved comparable machine learning performance to traditional methods. It enabled training a 12 billion parameter model across four U.S. regions using standard internet connectivity, completing training over 20 times faster than conventional synchronization techniques.

This architecture also allows mixing different hardware generations in a single training run, extending hardware utility and increasing compute capacity. Decoupled DiLoCo represents a step toward more flexible, efficient, and scalable AI training infrastructure that can leverage distributed resources globally.

output_cleanup.title: Google DeepMind releases DiffusionGemma, a 26B MoE model enabling up to 4x faster text generation on GPUs with parallel token processing
output_cleanup.description:
Google DeepMind introduced DiffusionGemma, an experimental open-source 26 billion parameter Mixture of Experts model that generates text up to four times faster on dedicated GPUs by producing entire blocks of tokens simultaneously rather than sequentially. The model targets speed-critical, interactive local workflows such as in-line editing and rapid iteration, operating efficiently within 18GB VRAM on consumer GPUs by activating only 3.8 billion parameters during inference.

DiffusionGemma uses a novel diffusion approach with bi-directional attention to refine text iteratively, allowing it to self-correct and handle non-linear text structures like code infilling and mathematical graphs. While its output quality is lower than standard autoregressive Gemma 4 models, it offers significant speed advantages for local inference scenarios, especially on single accelerators with low to medium batch sizes. Developers can fine-tune DiffusionGemma for specific tasks, as demonstrated by its improved performance on Sudoku solving due to its bi-directional attention mechanism.

The model has already seen over 150 million downloads across the Gemma 4 series, powering applications from wearable robotics to enterprise AI security.

output_cleanup.title: Researchers find nine popular AI coding tools vulnerable to HalluSquatting attack enabling large-scale botnets via hallucinated resource identifiers
output_cleanup.description:
Researchers have identified a new pull-based attack called HalluSquatting that exploits large language models' tendency to hallucinate resource locations, allowing hackers to assemble massive botnets and perform large-scale infections. The attack targets AI coding assistants and agents such as GitHub Copilot and Cursor, which routinely pull code from repositories and registries, by registering fake resource identifiers that LLMs are likely to hallucinate and seeding them with malicious instructions.

output_cleanup.description:
PrismML, a Caltech spinout, has reportedly compressed Alibaba's 27-billion-parameter Qwen 3.6 AI model from about 54GB to under 4GB, enabling it to run entirely on an iPhone 17 Pro with all parameters active simultaneously. This breakthrough challenges the assumption that large AI models require massive cloud infrastructure and could significantly impact on-device AI capabilities.

The compression relies on extreme quantization techniques, including 1-bit and ternary weight representations, which reduce memory usage and improve computational efficiency on mobile hardware. This approach supports faster inference, lower energy consumption, and enhanced privacy by processing data locally without cloud dependency. For Apple, such technology aligns with its focus on privacy, performance, and hardware-software integration, potentially advancing its AI strategy by enabling powerful AI models to run directly on consumer devices.

output_cleanup.title: Google and partners launch Agentic Resource Discovery Specification to enable AI agents to publish, discover, and verify tools and APIs across organizations
output_cleanup.description:
Google and industry partners have introduced the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) Specification, an open standard designed to help AI agents publish, discover, and verify external tools, APIs, and services across organizational boundaries. The specification addresses the lack of a common discovery and trust mechanism for widely distributed AI capabilities by establishing catalogs and registries that enable dynamic capability discovery while integrating with existing protocols like MCP and OpenAPI.

The ARD Specification includes domain-based ownership and verification mechanisms to ensure trust and reduce risk when autonomous agents interact with third-party services. Developed with contributions from Microsoft, GitHub, Hugging Face, Cisco, and others, early implementations such as GitHub’s Agent Finder and Hugging Face’s Discover Tool already leverage ARD for runtime capability discovery. The specification is available with reference implementations and aims to support multiple discovery services tailored to different indexing and governance needs.

output_cleanup.title: Apple sues OpenAI alleging former engineer exploited bug to steal trade secrets and accuses OpenAI of conspiring with ex-Apple employees
output_cleanup.description:
Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, claiming a former Apple engineer who joined OpenAI exploited a software bug to access and download confidential Apple files over several weeks. The complaint alleges that OpenAI conspired with former Apple employees to unlawfully acquire trade secrets to develop competing AI-powered hardware.

The lawsuit details how engineer Chang Liu used an authentication bug to access Apple's network after leaving the company, downloading sensitive information including unreleased product data and technical specifications. Apple also accuses OpenAI's chief hardware officer, former Apple executive Tang Yew Tan, of orchestrating a recruiting scheme to extract proprietary information from Apple employees during job interviews and "show and tell" sessions.

OpenAI disputes the allegations and says it is focused on building innovative technology without relying on other companies' trade secrets. Apple is seeking injunctions to prevent OpenAI from using the stolen information and is continuing its investigation into the extent of the alleged theft.

output_cleanup.title: Researchers adopt prompt injection as a defensive tactic called context bombing to disrupt AI hacking agents in simulated AWS environments
output_cleanup.description:
Researchers from Tracebit have developed a defensive technique named context bombing that uses prompt injections to cause malicious AI agents to shut down when encountering forbidden commands. Testing across five AI models in simulated Amazon Web Services environments showed this method significantly reduced successful attacks, cutting admin privilege escalations from 57% to 5% and complete compromises from 36% to 1%.

Context bombing builds on earlier work involving decoy AWS resources that alert defenders to AI attacks, aiming not just to detect but to stop attacks before they escalate. This approach leverages AI guardrails by embedding prompts that trigger refusal mechanisms in attacking models, effectively neutralizing their operations. Experts note this is the first known use of prompt injection as a defensive measure rather than an offensive tool.

A proposed class action lawsuit accuses SpaceX's Grok AI chatbot of enabling a man to create approximately 7,000 sexually explicit images of his underage stepdaughter by using a photo of her taken at age 11. The lawsuit highlights that Grok only reported a specific prompt involving "gang rape" to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), which led to authorities identifying the perpetrator. Despite this, the accused man later died by suicide after being released on bail, compounding the victim's trauma. The case also references prior incidents where Grok was used to produce millions of nonconsensual sexualized images, including those of children, raising broader concerns about the AI's misuse and the company's response to such abuses.

Symphony assigns an agent to each open task, allowing continuous autonomous work while humans review outputs, significantly reducing context switching and boosting productivity.

Symphony treats issue trackers as control planes, mapping each task to a dedicated agent workspace that runs until completion, automatically restarting stalled agents and managing task dependencies. This approach decouples work from individual coding sessions and pull requests, enabling agents to handle complex features, infrastructure migrations, and even generate new tasks based on discovered improvements, resulting in up to a 500% increase in landed pull requests on some teams.
